question: What does each layer need from the forward pass in order for backpropagation to work efficiently?
direct_answer: It needs enough saved intermediate information to compute local derivatives during the backward pass.
expanded_answer: Backprop is efficient because each layer stores values from the forward pass, such as inputs or activations, that are needed to compute derivatives of that operation. Without these saved values, the backward computation would have to recompute much more from scratch.
key_points: Local derivatives depend on stored values
common_wrong_ideas: The backward pass needs only the final loss value
No forward information is needed at all
Backprop stores every possible intermediate indefinitely
